content.value_statement: Statistical workflows often fail through poor model choice, weak diagnostics, or incorrect interpretation. This skill provides structured statsmodels guidance for reliable inference and forecasting.
actual_capabilities: Guides OLS, WLS, GLS, quantile regression, and robust standard error workflows.
Explains GLM family and link selection for binary, count, and positive continuous outcomes.
Covers logit, probit, multinomial, ordinal, count, and zero-inflated models.
Supports ARIMA, SARIMAX, VAR, decomposition, stationarity testing, and forecast evaluation.
Provides residual, influence, heteroskedasticity, autocorrelation, and normality diagnostics.
Helps compare models with AIC, BIC, likelihood tests, and out-of-sample validation.
limitations: Requires suitable data, Python, and the relevant statistical packages.
Does not guarantee valid inference when data quality or study design is weak.
Advanced models may require domain-specific assumptions beyond the provided guidance.
Users must review generated analyses before making consequential decisions.

use_cases.title: Analyze Research Data
use_cases.description: Select a model, test assumptions, estimate effects, and prepare interpretable statistical results.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Business Outcomes
use_cases.description: Model continuous, binary, categorical, or count outcomes with suitable diagnostics and validation.

use_cases.title: Forecast Time Series
use_cases.description: Assess stationarity, fit seasonal models, diagnose residuals, and compare forecast accuracy.

prompt_templates.title: Fit a Linear Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Fit an OLS model for [outcome] using [predictors]. Explain coefficient estimates, confidence intervals, model fit, and essential residual checks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a GLM
prompt_templates.prompt: My outcome is [outcome description]. Recommend a GLM family and link, explain the choice, and provide a diagnostic workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Forecast
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this time series setup: [data details]. Propose stationarity tests, candidate models, residual checks, and rolling forecast metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Complete Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible statsmodels analysis for [research question]. Include model alternatives, assumptions, robust inference, validation, effect interpretation, and reporting requirements.

output_examples.input: Compare Poisson and Negative Binomial models for overdispersed hospital visit counts.
output_examples.output: The response is count data, but the variance exceeds the mean. Fit both models, test dispersion, compare AIC, and report rate ratios.

output_examples.input: Review an ARIMA forecast for monthly sales with yearly seasonality.
output_examples.output: Test stationarity, inspect seasonal patterns, compare ARIMA and SARIMAX, check residual autocorrelation, and evaluate rolling forecast errors with prediction intervals.

output_examples.input: Explain a logistic regression result with a coefficient of 0.69.
output_examples.output: The coefficient is on the log-odds scale. Its odds ratio is approximately two, subject to confidence intervals and the model specification.

best_practices: Match the model family to the outcome distribution and research question.
Check assumptions, convergence, residuals, and influential observations before interpreting results.
Report effect sizes, uncertainty intervals, validation results, and important modeling decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not choose models only because they produce significant p-values.
Do not interpret coefficients before applying the correct link-function transformation.
Do not evaluate time series with shuffled cross-validation or future information.

faq.question: Does this skill execute statistical analyses automatically?
faq.answer: It provides structured guidance and examples. Execution depends on the available data, Python environment, and agent tools.

faq.question: Which regression models are covered?
faq.answer: It covers linear, generalized linear, discrete choice, count, ordinal, and several robust regression workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with time series forecasting?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers stationarity, ARIMA, SARIMAX, VAR, decomposition, diagnostics, prediction intervals, and forecast evaluation.

faq.question: Does it support causal inference?
faq.answer: It includes related methods and diagnostics, but credible causal claims still require appropriate study design and assumptions.

faq.question: Can it diagnose model problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It addresses heteroskedasticity, autocorrelation, non-normality, overdispersion, multicollinearity, outliers, influence, and convergence.

faq.question: Is statistical expertise still required?
faq.answer: Yes. Users should understand their data, verify assumptions, review generated work, and apply domain judgment.
